ai.title: Add minimal and none reasoning effort options to agent types
ai.summary: Extended reasoning effort enums in `AgentDefinition`, `OpenRouterReasoningOptions`, and `DynamicAgentDefinitionSchema` to include 'minimal' and 'none'. Updates cover core type definitions and OpenRouter SDK provider options. Ensures type consistency across agent templates and dynamic schema validation.

eli5.text: The system that decides how much an assistant 'thinks before answering' now accepts two new settings: one lets it do just the minimum thinking needed, and another tells it to skip the extra thinking entirely and answer right away. This affects anyone configuring an assistant's reasoning budget, so if you looked at the available options you would see 'minimal' and 'none' alongside the existing 'high', 'medium', and 'low' choices. Those two options are now live wherever assistants are defined or checked, so they can be picked today rather than just being planned.

ai.title: spawn-agent-utils.ts coerce null prompt to empty string
ai.summary: validateAgentInput in spawn-agent-utils.ts coerces null or undefined prompt to empty string before safeParse. Prevents throw on missing prompt when schema requires it. Scope: packages/agent-runtime. Mechanism: nullish coalescing operator ?? ''.

ai.title: Introduce base2-lite agent with grok-4.1-fast model
ai.summary: New `base2-lite` orchestrator variant added to `.agents/base2/`, configured with `x-ai/grok-4.1-fast` model and `commander-lite` sub-agent. This lite mode disables `write_todos` and `code-reviewer-opus`, delegating implementation to `editor-gpt-5` instead of heavy opus editors. `editor.ts` refactored into `createCodeEditor` factory supporting `gpt-5` and `opus` models, while `editor-lite.ts` moved to `.agents-graveyard/`. Scope covers internal agent definitions in `.agents/` directory.

eli5.text: An internal orchestrator now has a faster, lighter mode that uses a different AI model and skips some of the slower analysis steps, so certain automated coding tasks can run more quickly when full rigor isn't needed. The lite mode also swaps in a streamlined planning step and routes implementation work to a GPT-5-based editor instead of the heavier review process. This is a behind-the-scenes change for internal tooling that controls how the system breaks down and executes coding requests; if you rely on the older default flow, nothing about your experience changes. The new mode is in place today, but only takes effect when an internal process explicitly opts into it.

ai.title: Nightly buffbench eval switches to lite mode
ai.summary: evals/buffbench/main-nightly.ts replaces base2-fast and base2-fast-no-validation with base2-lite in the agents array. taskConcurrency drops from 5 to 3. Scope limited to nightly eval config; no user-facing surfaces affected.

eli5.text: The nightly internal testing run now uses a lighter-weight assistant configuration instead of the previous two faster ones, and it runs fewer tasks at the same time. Nothing you see or touch is affected; this only changes what the behind-the-scenes nightly test uses. If you were watching that test, you would see it pick the single lite setup and work with three tasks in flight rather than five.

ai.title: base2-editor agent added with pre-edit think phase
ai.summary: New `base2-editor` orchestrator agent delegates implementation to the `editor` agent via `useEditor` flag in `createBase2`. The `editor` agent prompt now mandates `<think>` tags before and between tool calls to enforce reasoning before implementation. Internal agent definitions in `.agents/base2/` and `.agents/editor/` updated to support this delegation and thinking constraint.

eli5.text: The system's internal assistant workflow now includes a required 'think first' step before making code edits. When you ask the assistant to edit code, it will pause and lay out its plan before writing anything, and a new orchestrator role has been added to route certain tasks through this more careful editor path. This applies to how the assistant processes your requests behind the scenes; if you use it today, you may notice a brief delay while it decides how to proceed before changes appear. The mechanism enforcing this is already live.

ai.title: Best-of-n agents think before selecting or implementing
ai.summary: Prompt changes in `best-of-n-selector.ts` and `editor-implementor.ts` require Sonnet/Opus agents to use extensive `<think>` tags before choosing or writing code. `editor-best-of-n.ts` reduces default parallel implementors from 4 to 3 (default) and 5 to 4 (max), while `base2.ts` forbids passing prompts to spawned editor agents. Selector output now mandates a short reason alongside the `implementationId`.

eli5.text: When multiple AIs are asked to draft a piece of code, the system now asks the 'picker' AI to think very carefully before choosing which draft to use, and asks each drafting AI to think hard before writing its draft. The number of drafts requested at once was lowered for the default case and for the maximum case. Finally, the picker's choice must include a short reason explaining why it picked that draft.

ai.title: Log OpenRouter error details in chat completions
ai.summary: Added `openrouterError` to the error logging payload in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts`. The handler now checks if the caught exception is an instance of `OpenRouterError` and serializes it via `toJSON()`. This provides specific upstream failure details for debugging chat completions requests.

eli5.text: When a request to use the chat assistant fails because the upstream AI provider (OpenRouter) had a problem, the system now records exactly what went wrong instead of a generic error. If you ever look at the logs for failed chat requests, you'll see the specific failure details returned by the provider alongside the usual error and request info. This affects anyone using the chat completions API when a provider-side error occurs, and it is live today.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes assistant that drafts edits for our team no longer offers the Gemini model as an option when running in its highest-ability mode. This only affects our internal staff when they use the max-power editor; anyone outside the company will not see a difference.

ai.title: CLI: simplify bash command handling
ai.summary: Refactored CLI bash command execution to remove AI context injection. Terminal commands now update UI history only, not LLM context. New `bash-messages.ts` utility handles message construction. Scope limited to `cli/src/utils/bash-messages.ts`, `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run a terminal command in the CLI, the command and its result are now shown in your chat history without being sent to the AI model for reasoning. Previously, bash commands were injected into the AI's context so it could react to them; now the system only updates your UI history. This affects the terminal command flow across the CLI, and you would notice that bash output no longer influences AI-generated text.
